1.why: Hedged, conditional claim; A/D are absolutes ('every kind', 'eventually'), B is a generic truism.

2.why: Classic paired-text answer shape: agrees with the aim, doubts the execution. Others are flat rejections/strawmen.

3.why: A third sentence typically corroborates the preceding anecdotal report with independent evidence; A is the only supporting-function option.

4.why: Undercutting the assumption behind a criticism is the standard function; D merely restates, B/C add objections a fourth sentence rarely does.

5.why: Preservation debates hinge on whether non-intervention saves or loses evidence; D is a factual, not evaluative, dispute.

6.why: Only option that reframes the transfer as fungus-serving rather than tree-to-tree altruism; B and D support the network, A is neutral.

7.why: 'Reverse the usual assumption' matches a purpose-of-text answer; B/C are overstated, D is a mere list.

8.why: Fill-in-the-blank contrast usually resolves to the sincere/substantive reading; the three others are cynical siblings of each other.

9.why: Three-move structural description (reject, resist collapsing, offer a third) is the nuanced one; the rest are single-move.

10.why: Distinguishes accuracy of recording from truth of what was recorded — the precise rebuttal to a verbatim-fidelity claim.

11.why: Persistence of a costly ornament is standardly explained by female preference; B removes a cost rather than explaining persistence.

12.why: Debunking-anecdote passages argue the story survives for what it flatters; A affirms the myth, C overstates.

13.why: Attacks the inference from trap counts (detection vs abundance) — the measurement-confound rebuttal.

14.why: Motive-attribution blank; 'bid for prestige' is the strategic reading that most such passages settle on over lapse/candor/contrition.

15.why: Opening with a failure sets up a reversal; the others generalize or moralize beyond a rhetorical-purpose answer.

16.why: 'Complicate' means add causes, not deny them; C and D overreach, A denies the record.

17.why: Vocab items test the less literal sense; 'moderate and restrained' over the weather meaning.

18.why: Reinterprets the productivity gain rather than denying it — the responsive, non-strawman option.

19.why: Valuable-but-insufficient is the hedged middle; A/B/D are extremes.

20.why: Counterintuitive 'first reinforced authority, democratized later' is the inference such passages support.

21.why: Archaic sense 'skill in handling'; the everyday meanings are the trap options.

22.why: The dissociation case (wolves present, willows still declining where water is deep) supports a non-wolf explanation; others support the standard cascade.

23.why: British/older sense 'plain and unadorned'; the homey senses are the familiar distractors.

24.why: Links the trait's spread to famine/disease pressure — a selective mechanism; B is modern correlation, C is counterevidence.
